topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This section introduces the lecture and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding cancer genetics and cellular transformation.

topics.label: Viral discovery of oncogenes and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for measuring cell transformation.

topics.label: Concepts and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major functional classes of cancer genes and illustrate how alterations in gene dosage and regulation affect cellular control pathways.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures in DNA repair, replication fidelity, and chromosome segregation produce genomic instability and trigger cellular stress responses in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step progression, hereditary predispositions, and tumor dynamics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cumulative genetic alterations drive multi-step cancer progression across sporadic cases, inherited predisposition syndromes, and evolving tumors.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This section concludes the lecture, offers suggested reading, and previews the next session.
